short_description: 150 printable play cards for ages 1–12, sorted by age and energy. Each has what you need, a talk line and a safety line. PDF in Letter and A4.
long_description:
150 printable play cards for ages 1–12, plus 36 summer and rainy-day cards. It is a PDF download in US Letter and A4.

When your child says “I’m bored,” pull a card and play. Most cards use things you already have: pots, socks, boxes and paper. 168 of the 186 cards need nothing to buy.

Each card has an age band and a starting age. It shows the energy level: calm, medium or wiggly. It lists what you need, prep time, mess and a rough play time. It gives short steps, one thing to say while you play, and a safety line. Cards for kids under 5 say “With a grown-up.”

A two-page grown-up guide shows how to start in two minutes. It has three talk tips and a pantry list. The card index gives an easier way, a harder way and a 2-minute tired-grown-up way for every card.

You also get 39 blank cards, card backs, 24 box dividers, 12 jar labels, a Play Menu, weekly planners and a fridge certificate.

You get five PDFs: START HERE, color and low-ink, each in Letter and A4. In the color files you can type in the blank cards, labels, dividers, planners and certificate. You can type text and tick circles. You can’t change fonts, colors or pictures.

Every play follows our published safety rules. This is a digital file. Nothing is shipped. For use in your own home.
bullets: 150 play cards in four age bands, plus 18 summer and 18 rainy-day cards. Each 60-page file has 8 guide pages, 25 card sheets and 27 pages of extras.
Every card shows the age band, a starting age, the energy level, prep, mess and play time, what you need, steps, a talk line and a safety line.
A 2-page grown-up guide, plus an easier, a harder and a 2-minute tired-grown-up version of every card.
Five plain PDFs: START HERE, color and low-ink, each in US Letter and A4. Type in the blank cards, labels, dividers and planners in the color files.
About 30 minutes to print and cut, then use them again and again. 150 plays, about 4¢ each. Every play follows our published safety rules.

compliance_notes: Rule 1: no health, medical, therapy, developmental or outcome claims; the last page says the cards are parent education, not medical or developmental advice. No diagnosis words in the product, images, keywords or tags. Rule 2: no company, app or device is named; the fill-in instructions say 'a free PDF reader that supports fill-in forms' and downloads say 'use a web browser, not the shopping app'. Rule 4 child safety, audited card by card (all 186): every card has its own safety line; every card for under-5s is flagged 'With a grown-up'; every Ages 1–3 card and every seasonal card that includes age 1 uses only things too big to fit through a toilet-paper tube (fixed in this audit: palm-size crayons instead of chunky crayons, a wide brush, big spoons and big cups, no sticks on the toddler nature walk); older cards with small things (coins, dice, tape, seeds, dough, shakers) say to keep them from under-3s; no balloons; no cords, strings, ties or long scarves (cloth strips are short; bags are paper or cloth); every water card says grown-up within arm's reach; no whole grapes, nuts, popcorn, hard candy or marshmallows, and snack cards use thin, soft pieces (cheese cubes removed); grown-ups handle knives, stove, oven, glass and tools. Every cut piece is 1.5 in or larger (cards 2.5 × 3.5, small labels 2.3 × 1.6, dividers 2.4 × 3.95, round labels 3.4); cut sheets print 'Grown-up keeps the pieces'; velcro is for ages 3+ with 'Check dots before each play; remove any that lift' and a no-dots route for under-3s. Rule 5: only the WHO 2019 under-5 guidelines are cited. Rule 6: talk tips in plain words, no program names. Rule 7 and logo: original titles, art and layout; supplied logo files only, one-colour white on grass, plum, sky and tomato, reverse on ink, primary on sun. Customer-voice rules: color + low-ink files in Letter and A4, plain PDFs under 15 MB, START HERE first, no URL or QR in Etsy files, version footer on every page, prep budget on page 1 and in the listing, prep/mess/time icons and starting age on every card, easier/harder and 2-minute versions for every card, 90% 'Nothing to buy', corner flags, no quiz or trivia cards (Family Trivia replaced by Clue Trail), 2-page grown-up guide with 'most children love 2–3 of these', home-language line, pediatrician line on the stage page, blank + pre-filled + fillable planners, labels and dividers. Small text is ink on white chips or tints (no white small text on tomato, sky or grass). Honest pricing: no anchor or 'was' price. AI-assisted content is never described as human-made.
